summary: Axios 1.21.0 meets the HTTP request requirement. It is the existing interceptor/global-config/mock client, it publishes through OIDC trusted publishing with SLSA provenance, its 27-package runtime tree is entirely MIT and has no install scripts, and a local CJS/ESM plus interceptor/mock probe passed. The residual risks are a single npm maintainer and a required follow-redirects pin with no provenance.
reasoning: Fit is direct: the requirement names axios interceptors, global configuration and mocking, and axios provides that surface in both browser and Node. Native fetch is explicitly out of scope for this request.

1.21.0 was published 2026-10-27, the repository was pushed 2026-10-28, and there are 146 published versions with 109,310 stars, so the project is actively releasing rather than coasting on past adoption.

The publish workflow is now verified: .github/workflows/publish.yml runs on v1.*.* tags with id-token: write, a protected npm-publish environment, SHA-pinned actions, npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm stage publish --provenance --access public.
The npm attestation for 1.21.0 resolves to the axios/axios repository, the publish workflow and the v1.21.0 tag, so the reviewed tarball is tied to the source commit.
The full runtime tree was installed and inventoried: 4 direct dependencies, 27 installed packages, 4.0 MB install, all 27 MIT, and no preinstall, install or postinstall scripts in any package.
OSV records no advisories for 1.21.0, and npm audit over the installed production tree reports zero vulnerabilities.
A local probe imported axios through both ESM and CJS, applied a global baseURL, a request interceptor and a response interceptor, and completed a mocked GET through a custom adapter.
The remaining release gap belongs to follow-redirects: it is the required Node transport beneath axios, has no npm provenance, and must be pinned at 1.16.2 with the gap recorded.
Footprint is moderate and now measured: 4.0 MB installed, 2,163 KB unpacked, and a dual CJS/ESM package with bundled types. Install size was previously unmeasured; it is no longer an open constraint.
caveats: Single npm maintainer (jasonsaayman) for a package with roughly 94M weekly downloads. Account compromise or maintainer burnout remains the main residual supply-chain risk; pin exact versions and commit the lockfile.
follow-redirects 1.16.2 is required by the Node adapter and has no npm provenance. Pin it exactly and record the gap.
All four dependency ranges are caret ranges, so two installs can resolve different transitive code. Use a lockfile or exact pins for the monitored stack.
No declared engines floor; check the supported Node range against the deployment runtime.
The 27-package tree is MIT and has no install scripts, but the browser bundle size was not measured; the 2,163 KB unpacked figure is not the shipped browser cost.
The repository carries 110 open issues, so triage latency for a future advisory is not evidenced by the clean current advisory record.

axios declares a prepare script for local development. It is not a preinstall/install/postinstall hook, and the verified publish workflow uses npm ci --ignore-scripts; do not treat it as an install-time execution path.
Native fetch remains out of scope for this requirement.

evidence.label: CI publish pipeline
evidence.detail: publish.yml runs on v1.*.* tags with id-token: write, environment npm-publish, actions/checkout and actions/setup-node pinned to commit SHAs, npm ci --ignore-scripts, and npm stage publish --provenance --access public.

evidence.label: SLSA provenance
evidence.detail: SLSA v1 attestation for 1.21.0: builder actions/runner/github-hosted, source axios/axios, workflow .github/workflows/publish.yml, ref refs/tags/v1.21.0.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: OSV returns no advisories for axios@1.21.0, and npm audit over the installed production tree reports zero vulnerabilities.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: 4 direct dependencies (form-data, proxy-from-env, follow-redirects, https-proxy-agent), 27 installed packages, 4.0 MB install, 2,163 KB unpacked. All 27 packages are MIT.

evidence.label: Install scripts
evidence.detail: axios itself declares no preinstall, install or postinstall hook, and the full 27-package runtime tree contains none. The prepare script is a local-development hook; the publish workflow runs npm ci --ignore-scripts.

evidence.label: TypeScript types
evidence.detail: Bundled declarations with dual CJS and ESM entries and an exports map; no separate @types package is required.

evidence.label: Runtime compatibility
evidence.detail: A local probe imported axios through both ESM and CJS, applied a global baseURL, request and response interceptors, and completed a mocked GET through a custom adapter. The package records dual browser/Node entries and no engines floor.

evidence.label: License
evidence.detail: axios is MIT and all 27 installed runtime packages are MIT. No copyleft or proprietary licence is introduced.

evidence.label: Maintenance
evidence.detail: 1.21.0 published 2026-10-27; repository pushed 2026-10-28; 146 versions; 109,310 stars; 110 open issues; single npm maintainer jasonsaayman.
